newsitem.title: USA: LCI in BellSouth local service pact.
newsitem.headline: LCI in BellSouth local service pact.

text.p: LCI International Inc said Wednesday it had agreed to a deal with BellSouth Corp that would enable the long-distance carrier to resell local phone services to customers across BellSouth's nine-state region.
In a statement, the company said it would initially focus on offering its brand of local phone service -- called Simply Direct -- to small and medium- sized businesses in the BellSouth region.
It said residential customers in the nine-state region would be able to select LCI as their local phone service carrier in the later half of 1997.

The deal with the regional Bell company allows LCI to re-sell BellSouth local service at a discount rate to customers in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina and Tennessee.

At the state level, LCI said it has submitted applications and received authority to provide local service in six of the states in the region, with applications to offer local phone service pending in Louisiana and North Carolina.
The company said it will soon apply to offer local service approval in Kentucky.

"Today's announcement is another step in the aggressive deployment of LCI's local telephone service strategy which aims to bring combined local and long distance service to both businesses and consumers by the end of the year," said Anne Bingaman, the new president of LCI's local service unit.
Bingaman was until recently the nation's top anti-trust regulator in the position of assistant attorney general at the U.S. Department of Justice's anti-trust division.

"While LCI will continue to negotiate resale agreements like this one with other local exchange carriers (LECs), our ultimate goal is to negotiate agreements that will allow us to sell the unbundled elements of ... local networks," she said.

"Unbundled" services would give LCI the chance to pick and choose which segments of the BellSouth's network it uses and also allow it to opt to install its own equipment. Such increased access to the local network would allow it to retain a larger portion of local service revenues over time.
LCI has rapidly grown in recent years to enter the ranks of the top six U.S. long-distance providers.
The resale agreement between LCI International and BellSouth is the first regionwide service agreement LCI has negotiated with one of the seven regional Bell companies.
